accumulation-of-change-s1.title: The velocity of a toy train
accumulation-of-change-s1.text: A toy train moves back and forth on a straight track. Its velocity $v(t)$, in feet per second, is positive when it moves forward. The graph is made of line segments.

plot.label: Graph of the velocity v(t) of a toy train in feet per second for t from 0 to 12 seconds, made of line segments

accumulation-of-change-s2.title: Pumping water into a pool
accumulation-of-change-s2.text: A pump changes the water in a pool at a constant rate during each period below. A negative rate means the pump is draining the pool. At $t = 0$ the pool holds 8000 gallons.

table.caption: Rate of change of the water in the pool, in gallons per hour, during each period of time t, in hours

items.q: By how many feet does the train's position change from $t = 0$ to $t = 6$ seconds?

mistakes.why: That is the top speed, 4 feet per second, times 6 seconds. The train only reaches that speed at $t = 2$; for the first 2 seconds the region under the graph is a triangle, not a rectangle.
That is only the rectangle from $t = 2$ to $t = 6$. Add the triangle from $t = 0$ to $t = 2$: $\frac{1}{2}(2)(4) = 4$ feet.

why.correct: The change in position is the area under the velocity graph. Triangle from 0 to 2: $\frac{1}{2}(2)(4) = 4$. Rectangle from 2 to 6: $4 \cdot 4 = 16$. Total: $4 + 16 = 20$ feet.

items.q: What are the units of the area of a region between this graph and the t-axis?
options: feet per second
feet per second per second
seconds
feet

why.correct: Area is height times width: (feet per second) $\times$ (seconds) = feet.
options: That is the unit of the height of the graph, the velocity. The area multiplies height by width, so the seconds cancel.
That is the unit of the slope of the velocity graph (acceleration), which divides by seconds instead of multiplying.
That is the unit of the width only. Area is height times width.
Feet per second times seconds is feet: the area measures a change in position.

items.q: Find the net change in the train's position, in feet, from $t = 0$ to $t = 12$ seconds.

mistakes.why: You added the area below the axis as if the train were still moving forward. From $t = 8$ to $t = 12$ the velocity is negative: the train backs up 6 feet, so subtract it.
That is the change only up to $t = 8$. From $t = 8$ to $t = 12$ the train backs up: a triangle of area 2 and a rectangle of area 4, 6 feet in all. $24 - 6 = 18$.

why.correct: Forward from 0 to 8: $4 + 16 + 4 = 24$ feet. Backward from 8 to 12: triangle $\frac{1}{2}(2)(2) = 2$ plus rectangle $2 \cdot 2 = 4$, so 6 feet. Net change: $24 - 6 = 18$ feet.

items.q: At what time in the interval from 0 to 12 seconds is the train farthest forward of where it started?
options: $t = 4$, in the middle of the time at top speed
$t = 8$, where $v$ turns from positive to negative
$t = 6$, where the velocity starts to decrease
$t = 12$, the right end of the time interval

why.correct: The position grows while $v(t) > 0$ (from 0 to 8) and shrinks while $v(t) < 0$ (from 8 to 12). It is largest at $t = 8$.
options: The flat part is where the speed is largest, but the train keeps moving forward after t = 4, so its position keeps growing.
Correct: forward motion adds to the position until t = 8, and after that every second takes some back.
From 6 to 8 the velocity is smaller but still positive, so the train is still moving forward and its position still grows.
After t = 8 the velocity is negative, so the train backs up: its position at 12 is 6 feet less than at 8.

items.q: How many gallons does the pump add to the pool from $t = 0$ to $t = 5$ hours?

mistakes.why: You added the two rates, 300 + 450. A rate must be multiplied by how long it lasts: 300 for 2 hours and 450 for 3 hours.
That uses 450 gallons per hour for all 5 hours. For the first 2 hours the rate was only 300.

why.correct: Each period is a rectangle under the rate graph: $300 \cdot 2 + 450 \cdot 3 = 600 + 1350 = 1950$ gallons.

items.q: How many gallons are in the pool at $t = 6$ hours?
options: 1830 gallons
10,070 gallons
9950 gallons
9830 gallons

why.correct: Amount at 6 = starting amount + net change $= 8000 + (600 + 1350 - 120) = 9830$ gallons.
options: That is only the net change. The pool started with 8000 gallons; add the change to the starting amount.
This adds the 120 gallons of the last hour, but the rate is negative then: the pump drains the pool.
This stops at t = 5. The last hour drains 120 gallons.

items.q: Which expression gives the change in the amount of water, in gallons, from $t = 2$ to $t = 6$?

why.correct: Gallons = (gallons per hour) $\times$ (hours) for each period: $450(3) + (-120)(1) = 1230$ gallons.
options: Subtracting the rates first treats both as lasting 4 hours. Multiply each rate by its own time.
This adds the 120 gallons of the last hour. The rate is negative then: the pump drains the pool, so that term is subtracted.
Correct: each rate times the length of its period, with the draining hour negative.
The rate 450 lasts only 3 hours (from 2 to 5), not 4.

items.q: On a graph of the rate against time, the region for $5 \le t \le 6$ lies below the t-axis and has area 120. What does it mean?
options: The pool gains 120 gallons, since an area is positive
The pool loses 120 gallons from t = 5 to t = 6 hours
The pool holds 120 gallons at t = 6 hours
The pump drains 120 gallons per hour at t = 6

why.correct: Area under a rate graph is an amount of change; a region below the axis is a decrease. From $t = 5$ to $t = 6$ the pool loses 120 gallons.
options: A region below the axis comes from a negative rate, so the amount decreases.
Correct: area means gallons, and below the axis means the amount goes down.
The area is a change over the hour, not the amount in the pool.
That is the height of the graph (a rate). The area is gallons, a rate times a time.

items.q: A drug enters the bloodstream at a rate $R(t)$, in milligrams per hour, where $t$ is in hours. What does the area under the graph of $R$ from $t = 0$ to $t = 3$ measure?
options: the milligrams of drug that enter during those 3 hours
the rate at which the drug enters at t = 3 hours
how fast the rate of entry itself changes over those 3 hours
the number of hours the drug takes to act

why.correct: The area under a rate graph is the amount accumulated: (milligrams per hour) $\times$ (hours) = milligrams.
options: Correct: milligrams per hour times hours gives milligrams.
That is the height R(3), in milligrams per hour, not an area.
That is the slope of the graph of R, in milligrams per hour per hour.
Hours are only the width; the area multiplies the height by the width.

items.q: A cart starts from rest and its velocity is $v(t) = 3t$ meters per second for $0 \le t \le 6$ seconds. How many meters does it move forward in those 6 seconds?

mistakes.why: That is the rectangle $18 \times 6$. The region under $v(t) = 3t$ is a triangle: take half.
That is $v(6)$, the velocity at the end, in meters per second. The distance moved is the area under the graph.

why.correct: The graph of $v$ is a line from $(0, 0)$ to $(6, 18)$, so the region under it is a triangle: $\frac{1}{2}(6)(18) = 54$ meters.

items.q: Tank A fills at a constant 5 liters per minute. Tank B fills at a rate that grows steadily from 0 to 10 liters per minute over the same 4 minutes. Which tank gains more water in those 4 minutes?
options: Tank A, because its rate is larger at the start
It depends on how much water each tank held at first
They gain the same amount, 20 liters each
Tank B, because its rate reaches 10 liters per minute

why.correct: A: $5 \cdot 4 = 20$ liters. B: a triangle, $\frac{1}{2}(4)(10) = 20$ liters. The amounts gained are equal.
options: A leads early, but B catches up. Compare whole areas, not rates at one time.
The question asks for the amount gained, which is the area under each rate graph, not the amount held.
Correct: a 4 by 5 rectangle and a triangle with base 4 and height 10 both have area 20.
B ends faster, but it starts at 0. Compare areas: B has a triangle of area 20, the same as the rectangle for A.

items.q: Water flows into or out of a tank at a rate $r(t)$ liters per minute, positive when water enters. From $t = 0$ to $t = 10$, the regions between the graph of $r$ and the t-axis have area 14 above the axis and 5 below. The tank held 30 liters at $t = 0$. How much does it hold at $t = 10$?
options: 9 liters
39 liters
49 liters
44 liters

why.correct: Net change = area above minus area below $= 14 - 5 = 9$ liters. Amount at 10 = $30 + 9 = 39$ liters.
options: That is the net change alone. Add it to the 30 liters already in the tank.
Correct: 30 + 14 - 5.
This adds the 5 liters, but the region below the axis is water leaving the tank.
This ignores the 5 liters that drain out.

items.q: The rate of change of the temperature of a cooling oven is negative for all $t$ between 0 and 20 minutes. What can you say about the temperature over that time?
options: It falls, by the area between the graph and the t-axis
It rises, because the area of any region is a positive number
It is a negative number of degrees at t = 20
It stays the same, since the rate has one sign

why.correct: A negative rate lowers the amount. The size of the drop, in degrees, is the area of the region between the rate graph and the t-axis.
options: Correct: the region lies below the axis, so its area is a decrease in degrees.
The size of the region is positive, but it lies below the axis, which means the temperature falls.
The rate tells the change, not the value. The oven can still be hot after it cools for a while.
A rate with one sign still changes the amount: a negative rate lowers it steadily.

items.q: Oil leaks from a pipe at a rate that rises steadily from 2 liters per minute at $t = 0$ to 8 liters per minute at $t = 6$ minutes. How many liters leak in those 6 minutes?

mistakes.why: That uses the largest rate, 8, for all 6 minutes. The rate starts at 2, so the region is a trapezoid, not a tall rectangle.
That uses the starting rate, 2, for all 6 minutes. The rate climbs to 8, so more leaks.
That is $(2 + 8) \cdot 6$. The area of a trapezoid is the average of the two heights times the width: halve it.

why.correct: The rate graph is a line from $(0, 2)$ to $(6, 8)$; the region under it is a trapezoid with area $\frac{2 + 8}{2} \cdot 6 = 30$ liters.

items.q: The rate of change of the temperature of a cup of soup is $H(t)$ degrees Fahrenheit per minute, $t$ in minutes. What does the area under the graph of $H$ from $t = 0$ to $t = 10$ tell you, if $H(t) > 0$ there?
options: how fast the temperature changes at t = 10 minutes
the number of degrees per minute that the soup gains on average
how many degrees the soup warms from t = 0 to t = 10
the temperature of the soup at t = 10 minutes

why.correct: Area under a rate graph = accumulated change. Here: degrees Fahrenheit per minute $\times$ minutes = degrees Fahrenheit gained over the 10 minutes.
options: That is H(10), the height of the graph, in degrees per minute.
That would divide a change by the 10 minutes; the area itself is the change in degrees.
Correct: degrees per minute times minutes gives a change in degrees.
The area is a change. The temperature at 10 also needs the starting temperature.

items.q: A cyclist rides on a straight path. Her velocity is positive from $t = 0$ to $t = 5$ minutes, where the region under the velocity graph has area 30 meters, and negative from $t = 5$ to $t = 7$, where the region has area 6 meters. Where is she at $t = 7$ compared with her starting point?
options: 30 meters ahead
24 meters ahead
36 meters ahead
6 meters behind

why.correct: Change in position = area above the axis minus area below $= 30 - 6 = 24$ meters, so she is 24 meters ahead of her start.
options: This is where she is at t = 5. She then rides back 6 meters.
Correct: 30 meters forward, then 6 meters back.
This counts the 6 meters as forward. Negative velocity means she rides back toward the start.
The 6 meters back come after 30 meters forward; she is still ahead of where she began.
